what: 2. The problem: total-indirect-effect tests have a blind spot
title: Power Enhancement for High-Dimensional Mediation: A Guided Tour
text: many mediators, conventional approach summarizes total indirect effect, written beta: sum mediators one’s individual indirect effect. global test checks whether beta = 0. works well mediators push outcome way. consider two active mediators whose individual indirect effects equal size opposite sign: say +0.5 M_1 -0.5 M_2. mediators genuinely active, yet contributions cancel, total indirect effect test built beta sees zero concludes “mediation,” even though two mediators plainly active. rare edge case: whenever different pathways move outcome opposite directions (heterogeneous mediation, extreme contrasting mediation), total indirect effect understates truth test loses power. article calls core limitation existing high-dimensional mediation tests.

what: 3. The idea: a power enhancement component
title: Power Enhancement for High-Dimensional Mediation: A Guided Tour
text: power-enhanced (PE) test fixes blind spot adding second piece cancel. penalized fit selects small set candidate-active mediators, PE component J_m adds , mediators, magnitude one’s combined path signal. code notation, alpha_hat[j] estimated M -> Y coefficient mediator j, Gamma_hat[, j] estimated X -> M coefficient exposure , se_* standard errors: Two things matter . First, indicator keeps mediator X -> M path M -> Y path individually significant, noise mediators contribute. Second, J_m sums absolute values, +0.5 mediator -0.5 mediator reinforce instead cancelling. full test statistic M_PE = S_n + J_m, benchmark Wald statistic S_n (total-indirect-effect test) plus enhancement. global null mediation, screen rejects every mediator, J_m = 0 M_PE behaves exactly like S_n (chi-square reference distribution, Type error rate). heterogeneous alternatives, J_m grows large test gains power. whole idea: keep size, add power exactly old test blind. indicator builds J_m also tells mediators active, familywise error rate control (default) false discovery rate control.
